Snippet.Description:
Watch Sir Antonio Pappano lead NYO-USA in a performance of Richard Strauss’s “Eine Alpensinfonie,“ Op. 64, at the Elbphilharmonie Hamburg in 2019.

NYO-USA 2019 comprised 119 members—ages 16–19 and hailing from 33 US states—who were recognized by Carnegie Hall as some of the finest players in the country following a comprehensive national audition process. In preparation for its performance activities in the New York area and abroad, NYO-USA once again worked with an impressive list of principal players from many of the nation’s top professional orchestras during its training residency. 
 
Following a return to the Tanglewood Music Festival in Lenox, Massachusetts, Sir Antonio Pappano and NYO-USA took the stage Carnegie Hall for the orchestra’s annual concert in Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage. The program included Strauss’s “Eine Alpensinfonie” and Berlioz’s “Les nuits d’été” featuring renowned mezzo-soprano Isabel Leonard. The orchestra then departed to Europe for debut performances as part of the Young Euro Classic series at Konzerthaus Berlin with mezzo-soprano Magdalena Kožená, as well as the Edinburgh International Festival and Elbphilharmonie Hamburg, and a return to the BBC Proms and Royal Concertgebouw Amsterdam with mezzo-soprano Joyce DiDonato.
Snippet.Title: NYO-USA Performs R. Strauss’s “Eine Alpensinfonie“

Snippet.Description:
Streamed live on 19 January 2024

Sir Antonio Pappano, newly appointed Chief Conductor Designate of the London Symphony Orchestra, makes his first appearance at the Royal College of Music since 2020.

Opening the programme, RCM Concerto Competition winners Méline Le Calvez and Francis Bushell take on Strauss‘ lyrical woodwind duet with orchestra, inspired by Hans Christian Andersen‘s tale The Princess and the Swineherd, and Madeline Boreham performs four of Strauss‘ most beautiful songs with orchestra.

Originally billed as a ‘symphonic poem‘, Mahler‘s First Symphony is epic in scale. Expanding from the gentle cuckoo calls of its opening to a funereal setting of Frère Jacques, the ‘lightning bolts‘ of the final movement bring the symphony to a valiant conclusion.

Sir Antonio Pappano - conductor
Méline Le Calve - clarinet
Francis Bushell - bassoon
Madeline Boreham - soprano
RCM Symphony Orchestra

R Strauss Duett-Concertino TrV 293
R Strauss Ständchen op 17 no 2
R Strauss Das Rosenband
R Strauss Freundliche Vision

The first in a series of French greats, performed by the RCM Symphony Orchestra under the direction of Sir Antonio Pappano, who holds an honorary doctorate from the College. Saint-Saëns' epic final symphony, dedicated to the memory of Franz Liszt, is as much a summation of its composers own career as it is a grand essay on symphonic form. Memorable themes, dazzling piano passages and an organ-led finale have made this work a concert hall favourite.

Snippet.Description:
Antonio Pappano and the Orchestra of the Royal Opera House perform the Overture from Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro (Le nozze di Figaro) during The Royal Opera: Live in Concert.  

David McVicar's production of Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro will be performed at the Royal Opera House 13 May–3 June 2026. Book now – https://www.rbo.org.uk/tickets-and-events/the-marriage-of-figaro-david-mcvicar-details 

The Marriage of Figaro is available to watch now – along with over 80 other extraordinary productions – on Royal Ballet and Opera Stream. Watch the whole performance now at https://www.rbo.org.uk/tickets-and-events/the-marriage-of-figaro-2022-digital  

The Royal Opera: Live in Concert features an outstanding cast performing much-loved classics of the opera repertory, joined by current Jette Parker Young Artists, 67 members of the Orchestra of the Royal Opera House and members of the Royal Opera Chorus,  performing together in person for the first time since we closed our doors to the public on 16 March. The concert is hosted by the BBC’s Katie Derham.

Enjoy this video? Subscribe to our channel to receive notifications about new ballet and opera clips.
Snippet.Title: The Marriage of Figaro - Overture (Mozart; Orchestra of The Royal Opera House, Antonio Pappano)

0:00:00 Haydn Symphony No. 100
0:25:19 Prokofiev Symphony No. 7
1:01:21 Encore: Khachaturian Waltz - Masquerade
1:07:05 Encore: Khachaturian Gayane Suite No. 1 - Lezginka

This video replaces the version I uploaded on 16 April 2026, which had an error in the processing from the original tape. This caused the Prokofiev and Khachaturian parts of the original recording to be copied at the wrong sample rate which very much affected the music and sound. I am very grateful that this issue was pointed out to me.

For those of you who have listened to the previous version of the recording, I must apologise if your enjoyment was in any way spoiled, and do hope you enjoy this version!

These performances were given during the 1996 BBC Proms Season as part of the Promenade Concert given on  9 August 1996 in the Royal Albert Hall, London. I am afraid I do not have the Schnittke Viola Concerto which was also performed during this concert.

This is part of a collection of live "off air" recordings from radio broadcasts I have made since 1970, and I have recently preserved by transferring from tape to digital format.
